title: Using AI and 90's text to speech to add voiceovers for my freeware game (demo video has audio)
author: JussiPKemppainen

comments.author: JussiPKemppainen
comments.body: a detailed description of what was done, how and why in the devblog:  [https://echoesofsomewhere.com/2023/09/25/ai-voiceovers/](https://echoesofsomewhere.com/2023/09/25/ai-voiceovers/)

replies.author: vedran-s
replies.body: Wow this is so awesome and artistic, love it! I am thinking of doing similar for my game, outsource some of the characters to voice actors and do some of the voices with the AI. But I’m not quite sure if I should go with it, given Steam and publishers are ridiculously so much against any use of AI. It might result in the game be banned from platform so not sure if it is worth it. Obviously since I am solo dev and finding the project from my own pockets can’t really afford a professional studio with voice actors for all characters.

replies.author: JussiPKemppainen
replies.body: these text to speech AI's have clean data which is not banned by Steam.

replies.author: vedran-s
replies.body: Ah okay, thanks for the reply! Good to know. There’s definitely a lot of paid / licensed services generated with AI and obtained from clean data, it would be crazy if they wouldn’t allow you to se that.

comments.author: phmsanctified
comments.body: I'm trying to develop my own game, would you mind sharing some prompts for rooms, aspect ratios, resolutions, etc? I'll forever be grateful

replies.author: JussiPKemppainen
replies.body: I have all my prompts on the project blog: https://echoesofsomewhere.com

replies.author: phmsanctified
replies.body: Would you be willing to share what aspect ratios/resolutions you used? The ironic thing is I've been on your site several times already today before your newest post

comments.author: JussiPKemppainen
comments.body: I really do not worry about the aspect ratio toomuch. I isually just start with 16:9 aspect ratio, but quicly veer away from that.

comments.author: IgnisIncendio
comments.body: The transitions are great! The music is, too.

comments.author: ThePilgrimSchlong
comments.body: Are the NPCs voiced by AI too?

replies.author: JussiPKemppainen
replies.body: Monst human NPCs are (some are actual humans). But robotic NPCs are voicee by Apple’s PlainTalk

comments.author: Bino-
comments.body: I checked out your blog, neat stuff! I've been thinking using Midjourney to generate some art for a game. How do you keep the generation consistent so that all the artwork looks the same? Nice stuff!

replies.author: JussiPKemppainen
replies.body: My prompts are as simple as possible. I am just relying on almost the out of the box midjourney look.

comments.author: Neo_futur_us
comments.body: Great work, should be an inspiration to anyone desperate to just get started in realising their dreams of games dev

comments.author: MartinDan98
comments.body: I saw this character somewhere on the YouTube. In some tutorial probably. Are you a creator of that tutorial?

comments.author: gibmelson
comments.body: Looks great, are you using static images for the scenes or is it 3-D?

replies.author: JussiPKemppainen
replies.body: Technically it is 3D. But practically static images. There are very detailed breakdowns at the project blog and a downloadable demo! https://echoesofsomewhere.com

comments.author: gibmelson
comments.body:
This is great. I'm actually trying to create a very similar type of game (point and click RPG hybrid) with the exact same approach static images + 3-D characters on top. 

Setting up collision detection and to make it match background graphics is kinda tedious, have you found a good workflow there?

Also love the transitions between scenes. 

Any plans to make the code open source? :)

replies.author: JussiPKemppainen
replies.body: All my custom code is open sourced. But I use commercial plugins & unity so I can not share everything the game needs. I use simple 3D meshes modeled from the location images to help with collisions & perspective. I have written about that as well in the blog
